moat_against: No network effects, low switching costs; fragmented competition (Wayfair, RH, Amazon, IKEA/mass)
Housing-cycle and big-ticket discretionary exposure — revenue fell in FY2023-24 when housing froze
Tariff/sourcing exposure on imported goods: Q2 FY2026 gross margin -160 bps on tariff costs
Premium multiple leaves no cushion: priced for growth the recent record (5-yr rev CAGR 2.8%) does not show
OE is working-capital volatile: FY2024 OCF flattered by a large inventory/WC release
moat_for: Premium brand portfolio (Pottery Barn, West Elm, Williams Sonoma) with in-house design
Largest omnichannel specialty home-furnishings player in a fragmented market; gaining share in a flat industry
Affluent (~$150k income) customer base, relatively resilient through cycles
Proven pricing power / full-price selling; operating margin up sharply vs pre-pandemic
Debt-free balance sheet, strong cash generation funding buybacks + rising dividend
B2B segment growing double digits (14.5% in Q2 FY2026), diversifying beyond housing turnover
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat (5/10): a portfolio of strong premium home brands (Pottery Barn, West Elm, Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn Kids/Teen, Rejuvenation) with in-house design, an omnichannel digital-first model, an affluent customer base, and proven full-price selling that expanded operating margins sharply since pre-pandemic and is gaining share in a flat, fragmented industry (no player >5%). But there are no network effects and low switching costs, competition is fragmented and relentless (Wayfair, RH, Amazon, mass retailers), demand is housing-cycle driven, and imported sourcing leaves margins exposed to tariffs — Q2 FY2026 gross margin fell 160 bps on tariff costs. Durable brand/operational edge, not a wide structural moat; CAP 8.5 years.
name: Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality premium home retailer, moat 5/10, but at $239.84 it does not clear 15% — weighted IRR 6.8%, weighted IV@15 $82.08; it would need to fall to ~$82 (the weighted IV@15) to clear the 15% hurdle.
